title: Mysore Traditional Paintings
description: Classical painting school distinguished by delicate brushwork, muted mineral tones, and raised zinc-oxide gesso work gilded with 24-karat gold leaf (Swarna Patra).
altText: Artisan applying mineral pigments and gold-leaf gesso work to a traditional Mysore painting.
historicalBackground: Originated from the Vijayanagara school and patronized extensively by the Wadiyar court; registered under GI Application No. 32 (Certificate No. 26, January 2006).

title: Yakshagana Dance-Drama
description: Traditional all-night coastal Karnataka musical theatre uniting Bhagavata singing, chande and maddale percussion, extempore dialogue, and carved kirita headgear.
altText: Yakshagana performer backstage adjusting an ornate golden kirita crown under oil-lamp light.
historicalBackground: Documented by the Sangeet Natak Akademi under India's national inventory of traditional performing arts, spanning Badaguthittu and Tenkuthittu styles.

title: Dollu Kunitha
description: Energetic ritual drum dance performed by Kuruba folk troupes carrying cylindrical hollow dollu drums, prominently featured in state Dasara processions.
altText: Karnataka Dollu Kunitha drummers performing synchronized dance choreography with cylindrical drums.
historicalBackground: Patronized by the Karnataka Janapada Academy and featured officially in the Mysuru Dasara Jambu Savari procession.

title: Mysore Silk
description: Pure mulberry silk sarees woven with gold and silver zari by Karnataka Silk Industries Corporation (KSIC) looms in Mysuru.
altText: Folded pure mulberry Mysore silk sarees with gold zari borders beside regional Karnataka crafts.
historicalBackground: Founded under Maharaja of Mysore patronage and protected under Geographical Indication Application No. 22 (registered 2005).

title: Channapatna Toys & Dolls
description: Lathe-turned ivory-wood (Wrightia tinctoria) toys colored with safe vegetable dyes and natural shellac polish in Channapatna.
altText: Hand-turned Channapatna lacquered wooden toys displayed on an artisan workbench.
historicalBackground: Historical craft lineage traces back over two centuries to Tipu Sultan; registered under Geographical Indication Application No. 23 (2006).

title: Bidriware Metalcraft
description: Cast zinc-copper alloy vessels inlaid with pure silver (tarkashi) and oxidized to a matte black finish using Bidar Fort soil.
altText: Silver-inlaid blackened Bidriware vessel crafted in Bidar, Karnataka.
historicalBackground: Developed in Bidar and registered under Geographical Indication Application No. 21 (2006).

title: Kodagu Devarakadu (Sacred Groves)
description: Traditional sacred forest patches ('God's forests') guarded by ancestral village taboos against tree felling, protecting biodiversity and springs.
altText: Moss-covered stone shrine preserved inside a dense Western Ghats sacred grove in Kodagu.
historicalBackground: Preserved across Kodagu through community temple committees in co-management with the Karnataka Forest Department.
